doc.title: Jon Hendricks interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]

title: The story of 'Cloudburst' and Leroy Kirkland as Claude Cloud
summary: Hendricks tells how Leroy Kirkland and Benny Harris wrote Cloudburst, recorded as Claude Cloud and his Thunderclaps; Sam the Man Taylor played the solo.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: If I can jump back for one minute — I have to ask you about “Cloudburst.” I mean the song “Cloudburst” was that based on a Wardell Gray solo?

No, no. That’s a tragic story. Because you know, all of the guys that came out of the band when the big bands began to break up, you know Chic Webb’s band, all of them went into some aspect of the music business to try to continue to make a living with music. And Chic Webb’s guitarist, his name was Leroy Kirkland. And he was one of Chic Webb’s main arrangers you know, a fine musician. And he was around Broadway trying to make a living selling songs, writing songs, conducting rhythm & blues recording dates you know, doing anything he could. And he finally got a gig from MGM Records that wanted him to do an album of great rock type, rhythm & blues type, flag waving type songs. And so he thought this was beneath him. But the money was good. So he figured okay, he would make this album. And there was a song that he wanted to record on the album called “Cloudburst” that was written by two great jazz musicians, Leroy himself and a trumpet player named Benny Harris who was a legendary trumpet player and played with Dizzy, played with Bird for a while, but died of an overdose very early. But a very hip musician. And they wrote this song called “Cloudburst.” So he figured well since some part of the tune, I wrote part of it, I’ll call the album “Cloudburst” and I’ll call myself “Claude Cloud” and I’ll call the orchestra “the Thunderclaps.” So it was “Claude Cloud and his Thunderclaps,” with the album featuring “Cloudburst.” And he felt well that’d be a good place to hide — whoever heard this album and decided, oh, man, what is Leroy doing? And it was a smash hit. So poor Leroy Kirkland collecting all that money, and very sad because all these years of struggle, nobody still knows his name.
He pulled a fast one on himself.
You know we used to joke when we saw him, we’d say, “Claude” — he’d say, “don’t!”
But that solo you did on that tune goes by —
Sam the Man Taylor is the one that played that.
